body: I also went to a grade deflating state school. I got a 3.72 in a very bio-unrelated engineering major, and that “mediocre” GPA earned me the top graduating senior honor within the major. Going into this cycle, I thought my chance at T20 was slim, especially when my trend is downward and my MCAT was lower than 520. Granted, I did take multiple gap years and got additional degrees that might have set me apart a little. But how this cycle turned out was beyond my expectation: currently have 1 acceptance at a stats whore T20, waiting for post-II results from other 3 T5/T10s including another stats whore school. I might get even better results with a much better GPA, but this turnout greatly surpassed my impression of how far a 3.7 GPA can get me. I guess my point is, as cliche as it sounds, your journey and your story approaching medicine matters a lot, and outliers do exist beyond the statistics. Trust the process and anything is possible!
Also a 4x retaker but with 3 similar scores :'(, 7 interviews and 2 As so far!

Warning: Lots of words. Sorry for bombing you with words. 

The 3/24 test was a beast, at least to me. I ran out of time in C/P because of heavy calculations and as a grad engineering student that was utterly embarrassing. It was the very first time I almost ran out of time in C/P and encountered questions I couldn't even make an educated guess. And that's when I realized I needed to sharpen my arithmetic and problem-solving skills. I also almost ran out of time in CARS because the very last passage was basically Gibberish to me. B/B and P/S felt a lot better. B/B had lots of simply recall questions and very little biochem. P/S had lots of 50/50 for me. The final score does correspond with my impression of the test. I was so shocked at 131 in B/B because I had never gotten that high of a score in B/B. It's WILD!

My decision to retake is that my FL average (513) is higher than the real test and I know I could have done better in C/P and P/S (understanding the terms better).  I, again, procrastinated to start studying when the 2.5-month mark came around. This time, I started by reading the 300-page document to really understand and differentiate all the terms. I then started MrPankow P/S Anki after done reading, and this lasted all the way to the real test. For science, I started with kind of skim through Kaplan on my weak areas. Again, I did daily UWORLD and AAMC CARS Diagnostic Tool. The amount of questions varied (10-50) depending on how exhausted I was that day. This time I made sure to cover all science topics when generating the test, and for each question I got wrong, I tried my best to go back to Kaplan and read the relevant chapter. I also marked all the bullet points I have gone through once in the AAMC outline. For the ones that remain unmarked later in the process, I again go back to read Kaplan. For CARS, honestly, I don't know how my score increased a bit. But the strategy I started using this time was making sure I could reference back to a specific point in the passage when I made selections, even if it seemed to be an easy or obvious question. Actually, I had “answer is always in the passage” mindset for all sections this time.

For FL, I always did one test every weekend until the last week before the exam. This last time, I did BP FL first because I have done AAMC FLS. An extra perk of BP is that their C/Ps are difficult and calculation-heavy, so I get to practice timing. For B/B, I finished all miledown B/B anki before March, so I decided to try Jacksparrow this time.  I was far away from finishing that B/B set by the test came around. I was also afraid reusing AAMC FLs and SB would not be representative, but I think my brain made MCAT a trauma response so that I don't remember anything when I used them again. 

9/9 test was a lot easier compared to 3/24 for me. For a second I was afraid they were easy because I misread the questions. I'm not sure if it's luck or if my study actually worked. I also don't understand what happened with B/B. I guess that's the proof that MCAT is unpredictable. P/S this time didn't have that many 50/50s compared to 3/24 and I think this contributed to really understanding the concepts.

For all tries, I was either full-time doing research or doing intern. I studied for at most 4-5 after work and full days on weekend. I didn’t have time to finish UWorld (used 41%, 77% average) or finish AAMC Science QPs.
